summary: Malicious party submits Paillier key violating biprime structure (N = p*q*r instead of p*q). After signing ceremony, adversary uses multi-prime factorization to decrypt other parties' k_j shares from MtA proofs, reconstructs private key.

c-split variant TSSHOCK class. Thorchain's go-tss fork applied 2022 α-shuffle fix narrowly. c-split sibling variant remained — adversary bonded validator (~5M RUNE), participated in TSS signing ceremonies, sent malformed ZK proofs that c-split-extracted Asgard vault private key offline. Drained 4 chains for $10.8M.
lesson: Paid bounty fix often closes ONE instance of a class. Sibling variants must be checked separately for years after.

summary: GG20 MtA range proof verification flaw — malicious party can convince honest party that share is in valid range when it's not. Cascade to incorrect signature aggregation, key recovery in edge cases.
FROST signing ceremonies where nonce derivation does not bind session ID → if adversary observes 2 partial signatures with same nonce, recovers signer's secret share.

Lazarus group compromised 5 of 9 Ronin validator nodes (4 directly + 1 via Sky Mavis's RPC node accepting requests on behalf of Axie DAO). NOT a crypto bug — operational + threshold-too-low. $625M loss. Lesson: bonded-actor threat model applies even where crypto is sound.

Multichain CEO unilaterally controlled MPC key shares (concentration of trust). After CEO arrested by Chinese authorities, $130M drained. NOT crypto bug — governance / custody bug. Lesson: when reviewing MPC bridges, audit not just the math, but who-controls-what-share.

Wormhole Solana side `complete_transfer_wrapped` accepted a `signature_set` account without checking that it was created through the legitimate guardian-verification path. Attacker created a fake signature_set account via deprecated `post_vaa` without real guardian signatures, then called complete_transfer_wrapped with this fake set. Bridge minted 120,000 wETH out of nothing. Root cause class: cryptographic verification path bypass — bridge trusted attested payload (signature_set) without verifying account provenance. Fix was narrow (validate signatureSet creator) — siblings of the same class may exist in post-fix code.

A routine upgrade of the Nomad Replica contract set the default trusted merkle root to `0x00`. Function `process()` accepted any message where `messages[messageHash] == 0x00` (treated as confirmed). Attacker copied a legitimate withdrawal message, replaced the recipient address, retransmitted — passed validation. Free-for-all in the open mempool: hundreds of users copied the exploit tx and drained it to zero themselves. Root cause class: trusted-state initialization gap — bridge trusts default state as a valid attestation. Fix: emergency revert + redeploy. Siblings: any protocols using sentinel zero values for 'trusted'.

Verus-Ethereum bridge `submitImports()` (selector 0x8c49b257) correctly verified: (1) 8/15 notary signatures over Verus state root, (2) Merkle proof of cross-chain export inclusion, (3) hash binding to the serialized transfer blob. Did NOT verify: source amount conservation (sum burned/locked on Verus >= sum paid out on Ethereum). Attacker created a CCE with $0.01 VRSC input and $11.58M output instruction (1,625 ETH + 103.6 tBTC + 147K USDC), notaries signed cryptographic integrity (not semantic), `_createImports` decoded the blob and paid out. Root cause class: cryptographic verification ≠ semantic verification — missing `checkCCEValues` function (~10 lines Solidity to fix per Blockaid). Funding: 1 ETH via Tornado Cash hours before the exploit. Single-tx exploit. Wallet 0x5aBb...D5777.

Pattern documented by Cantina (not specific incident): UserOp hash derivation uses calldata-based shortcuts (packed encoding without domain separation). If 2 different accounts have identical bytecode (factory-deployed clones), a UserOp signature on account A may be valid on account B → cross-account replay. Root cause class: hash construction does not include unique account-specific entropy (account address as part of domain separator). Fix pattern: ensure entryPoint + chainId + account address baked into hash domain.

Pattern documented by Cantina: smart account implements ERC-1271 `isValidSignature(hash, sig)` without proper EIP-712 domain separation. A signature created for context A (e.g., Uniswap order) may be replayed in context B (e.g., Permit2 transfer) if the hash structure is not unique. Root cause class: ERC-1271 imp trusts caller-provided hash without verifying intent context. Fix pattern: EIP-712 domain separator with chainId + verifyingContract + intent-specific typed data.

Pattern documented by Cantina: paymaster sponsors gas without an upper bound per-user / per-time-window OR the postOp callback uses state that changed between validation and execution. Attacker spams UserOps with max gas, drains paymaster deposit. Variant: paymaster checks balance in `validatePaymasterUserOp`, but `postOp` recalculates cost using fresh state (e.g., gas price spiked) — paymaster eats difference. Root cause: validation-execution state drift + missing per-account budget. Fix pattern: hard limits per UserOp + per account/time + frozen pricing snapshot between validation and postOp.

Pattern documented by Cantina: account factory uses CREATE2 with a salt that is not cryptographically bound to the initial owner (e.g., only nonce). Malicious bundler observes user's first UserOp (initCode + intended initial state), front-runs deployment with a different init state (e.g., different owner address), occupying the counterfactual address. User's address is now deployed by attacker → denial-of-wallet OR funds locked if they were already sent to the counterfactual. Root cause: CREATE2 salt does not commit to owner identity. Fix pattern: salt = keccak256(owner_pubkey || ...) — only the owner can deploy their address.
